solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Short man drove into woman's tropical tree

indicators.note: short means the word for a man loses its final letter

parts.note: Jack is a man's name

indicators.note: into means the driving word goes inside the woman's name

parts.note: Ada is a woman's name
drove means ran, as a car or a bus service ran

explanation.surface: A little man drives his car into a woman's tropical tree.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drove' looks like a car journey, but it is the past of run, the piece that 'into' sends inside the woman's name.
explanation.definitionFit: The jacaranda is a tropical American tree with blue-violet flowers, so this is an example of the category.

clue.text: One who showed patience penning a hundred sheep

indicators.note: penning means enclosing, as sheep are shut in a pen

parts.note: Job of the Bible is proverbial for his patience under suffering
C is the Roman numeral for a hundred

explanation.surface: A patient shepherd pens a hundred sheep.
explanation.walkthrough: 'penning' puts AC inside JOB.
explanation.definitionFit: The Jacob is a piebald breed of domestic sheep, named after the Biblical patriarch's spotted flock.

clue.text: Woman on lorry releasing repressed emotions

parts.note: Cath is a short form of the woman's name Catherine
an artic is an articulated lorry, a British truck with a hinged trailer

explanation.surface: A woman riding on a lorry lets her pent-up feelings out.
explanation.walkthrough: ARTIC is British shorthand for an articulated lorry, a large truck.
explanation.definitionFit: Catharsis is the purging of pent-up feelings, so something with that effect frees bottled-up emotion.

clue.text: Again treat golfer, perhaps, during vacation

indicators.note: during means the golfer comes in the middle of the holiday break

parts.note: a recess is a vacation, as of Parliament or a court
a golfer may be a pro, a professional player

explanation.surface: A golfer gets treated again while on holiday.
explanation.walkthrough: 'vacation' in the sense of a break from sitting, as Parliament or the courts take, not a trip away.
explanation.definitionFit: To process is to handle material, so doing it a second time is to treat it once more.

clue.text: Latest tax on cord worn by leader of detectives — here?

parts.note: the latest thing is the new one
scot is an old word for a tax, as in scot-free

indicators.note: worn by means the cord goes round the detectives' leader, as a lanyard hangs on a person

parts.note: a lanyard is a cord worn round the neck

indicators.note: leader of means only the opening letter of detectives is used

explanation.surface: A new levy is placed on the cord the chief detective wears: where would that be?
explanation.walkthrough: SCOT is an old word for a tax (as in scot-free). The answer is the London Metropolitan Police headquarters, so the whole clue points to where detectives work.
explanation.definitionFit: The clue is all about detectives, and their London police headquarters is the place meant by this word.

clue.text: Publicised drink taken by reservist's best friend?

indicators.note: taken by says the drink is held by the reservist, the reservist's word coming last

parts.note: a view publicised is aired
ale is a drink, beer
a terrier is a member of the Territorial Army, Britain's volunteer reserve force

explanation.surface: A soldier from the reserves is given a drink while it is announced who his best friend is.
explanation.walkthrough: TERRIER is slang for a member of the Territorial Army, Britain's part-time reserve force.
explanation.definitionFit: The dog is called man's best friend, and this is a breed of large terrier, so the question mark marks an example.

clue.text: Degree of elevation that's perfect for some players

definitions.meaning: the steepness of a roof is its slope or angle
musicians may have perfect ___, naming a note without a reference

explanation.surface: Some musicians have a perfect ear for the height of a note.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means a roof's slope, and perfect ___ is the gift of recognising musical notes unaided.

clue.text: Works of art positioned on this regularly

parts.note: positioned means put in place

indicators.note: regularly means every other letter of this is taken

explanation.surface: Artworks are set on this place at intervals.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly' takes T and I from 'this'.
explanation.definitionFit: These are the chubby cherub figures in Renaissance paintings and sculpture, so they are artworks themselves.

clue.text: Not necessarily thick, this malefactor

parts.note: the saying thick as thieves means close friends, but a criminal need not be thick, meaning stupid

explanation.surface: A wrongdoer who is not necessarily stupid.
explanation.walkthrough: Plays on the idiom 'thick as thieves' (very close friends): 'thick' also means stupid, and a robber need not be.
explanation.definitionFit: A malefactor is a wrongdoer, and a robber who steals is a classic criminal of that kind.

clue.text: Plant cardinal finally dropped in consecrated wine?

indicators.note: dropped in means the cardinal's last letter falls inside the consecrated word

parts.note: consecrated means made holy

indicators.note: finally means the last letter of cardinal

parts.note: hock is a German white wine from the Rhine

explanation.surface: A cardinal finally pours some consecrated wine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cardinal' suggests a churchman with communion wine; only its final letter is used. Hock is the British name for German Rhine wine.
explanation.definitionFit: The hollyhock is a tall garden flower of the mallow family, an example of the category.

clue.text: Dupe whip's assistant at Westminster primarily

parts.note: the cat, the cat-o'-nine-tails, is a whip
a PA is a personal assistant

indicators.note: primarily means the first letter of Westminster

explanation.surface: A party whip's assistant in Parliament is someone's fool.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Whip' and 'Westminster' suggest a parliamentary whip; here the whip is the cat, a lash.
explanation.definitionFit: A person used as a tool by another, after the fable of the monkey using a cat to pull chestnuts from a fire.

clue.text: Note about recorder originally employed in genuine court action

indicators.note: employed in means that group sits inside the genuine word

parts.note: genuine means real

indicators.note: about means the note wraps round the recorder's first letter

parts.note: ti is a note of the sol-fa scale

indicators.note: originally means the first letter of recorder

explanation.surface: A note about a recorder is used in an authentic legal action.
explanation.walkthrough: A recorder is also a part-time judge in England, which pulls toward the court; here only its first letter is wanted, and the note is the sol-fa ti.
explanation.definitionFit: A second hearing of a case is a legal proceeding, so a fresh trial is an action in court.

clue.text: Presumably vote against party

parts.note: someone voting against would presumably ..., so this word stands for be a
a no is a vote against

explanation.surface: Someone is expected to vote against a party.
explanation.walkthrough: Split the letters as BE A NO: what you are when you vote against something.
explanation.definitionFit: A British informal word for a lively celebration or knees-up.

clue.text: Insect a theologian is canny about at the start

indicators.note: at the start means the word for about comes first

parts.note: c, from circa, means about
DD is a Doctor of Divinity
fly is slang for canny, shrewd and knowing

explanation.surface: A shrewd theologian goes on about an insect from the start.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at the start' places C first.
explanation.definitionFit: The caddis fly is a moth-like winged creature whose larvae build protective cases underwater.

clue.text: Wash in club at Hendon

indicators.note: in means the letters are found inside the words club at Hendon

explanation.surface: A wash at the club in Hendon, a north London suburb.
explanation.definitionFit: To wash oneself or soak in water is to immerse, as in a bath.

clue.text: Plundering of fat bloke securing rights in different places

indicators.note: securing means the fat bloke's name holds the rights inside it

parts.note: big means fat
R is short for right; rights gives two of them, one used in each name

indicators.note: in different places says the two right letters go into separate spots, not side by side

parts.note: Andy is a man's name, any bloke

explanation.surface: A fat man is robbed of his rights in several places.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fat bloke' becomes a nickname, Big Andy; 'in different places' tells you the two R letters do not sit together, each name taking one.
explanation.definitionFit: Brigands are bandits, so their activity is robbery and pillage, the plundering of travellers.

clue.text: Sort of lens hotel poet developed

indicators.note: developed means the letters are worked into a new form, as film is developed

explanation.surface: A photographer's lens developed by a poet at a hotel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'developed' fits a camera surface, but signals the anagram of HOTEL POET.
explanation.definitionFit: This kind of lens magnifies distant subjects, a long-focus camera lens type.

clue.text: Heat stops circulating at great speed

indicators.note: circulating means moving round, so the letters move into a new order

explanation.surface: The heat stops going round very quickly.
explanation.definitionFit: The adverb means with all haste, as fast as the old post riders could go.

clue.text: Laugh uproariously after deliveries go too far

indicators.note: after means the laughing word follows the deliveries

parts.note: an over is a set of six deliveries in cricket
to hoot is to laugh loudly

explanation.surface: Someone laughs loudly after several balls overshoot the mark.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket an over is a set of six balls bowled, or deliveries.
explanation.definitionFit: To pass beyond a target or limit is to exceed it, as a plane past the runway.

clue.text: Endless mysterious instances

indicators.note: mysterious means the letters are puzzling, set in an unexpected order

explanation.surface: Mysterious cases that never end.
explanation.definitionFit: Never ceasing means without stop, so unending and ceaseless are synonyms.

clue.text: Reportedly risk the meat course?

indicators.note: reportedly means the word for risk is heard rather than read

parts.note: a stake is the money you risk on a bet

explanation.surface: Is the main meat dish said to be a gamble?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reportedly' signals a sound-alike: the gambler's STAKE.
explanation.definitionFit: A thick slice of beef grilled or fried is the main item of a meal, its meaty dish.

clue.text: Ratings deceived a talked-of person on the run

parts.note: ABs, able seamen, are naval ratings

indicators.note: talked-of means the words are judged by how they sound when spoken

parts.note: deceived is conned, so the words give conned a

explanation.surface: Sailors were tricked by a much-discussed fugitive.
explanation.walkthrough: Ratings are ordinary sailors; ABS is able seamen. 'talked-of' makes 'conned a' sound like CONDER.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who escapes custody or flees is a fugitive, one who has run away.

clue.text: Ancient kingdom identified by female graduate

parts.note: she is the female pronoun
a BA is a Bachelor of Arts graduate

explanation.surface: An old realm was identified by a woman with a degree.
explanation.definitionFit: This was the Biblical realm in southern Arabia whose queen visited Solomon.

clue.text: Like one welcomed into sailor's watering-hole

indicators.note: welcomed into means taken inside the sailor's word

parts.note: OS is an ordinary seaman, a sailor
as means like
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Someone is welcomed into a sailor's local pub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'welcomed into' puts ASI inside OS. 'Watering-hole' suggests a pub; here it is desert water.
explanation.definitionFit: A fertile spot in a desert with a spring is a place where animals and travellers drink.

clue.text: One who entertains head of automobile plant

parts.note: a host is someone who entertains guests

indicators.note: head of means just the opening letter of automobile

explanation.surface: A host drives the boss of a car factory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'plant' suggests a factory with an automobile boss; it is the garden plant.
explanation.definitionFit: A shade-loving leafy garden perennial is an example of the category.

clue.text: Eurasian tree the council finally planted in Lincoln

indicators.note: planted in means the letters are set inside the president's name

parts.note: Abe Lincoln, the US president

indicators.note: finally means the last letters of the and council

explanation.surface: The council has planted a tree in Lincoln.
explanation.walkthrough: 'finally' takes E and L, and 'planted in' sets them inside ABE. Lincoln suggests the English city.
explanation.definitionFit: The white poplar has this alternative name, a species found across Europe and Asia.

clue.text: Fellow European holds record, taking on a form of diving

indicators.note: holds means the fellow's name contains the record

parts.note: Des is a man's name, any fellow
an EP is an extended-play record

explanation.surface: A man from Europe holds a record in a kind of diving.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fellow European' reads as one person from another country, but it splits into a man's name, Des, and the abbreviation for European.
explanation.definitionFit: This describes diving far below the surface in the open ocean, a kind of underwater exploration.

clue.text: Popular Arab advancing first of ships near coast?

parts.note: in means popular, fashionable

indicators.note: advancing means the letter moves forward to the front of the horse word

parts.note: an Arab is a breed of horse

indicators.note: first of means only the opening letter of ships counts

explanation.surface: A popular Arab leads the ships close to land.
explanation.walkthrough: 'advancing' moves the S of HORSE to the front, making SHORE.
explanation.definitionFit: Close to land, toward the shoreline: the adjective describes waters near the coast.

clue.text: He won the Nobel prize for literature? Indeed, way back

definitions.text: He won the Nobel prize for literature?

parts.note: yea means yes, indeed

indicators.note: back means the street abbreviation is read in reverse

parts.note: St is short for street, a way

explanation.surface: Did he win the Nobel literature prize? Yes, long ago.
explanation.walkthrough: 'way back' suggests long ago; it turns ST round. The question mark marks one example of a laureate.
explanation.definitionFit: The Irish poet W B ___ received the literature award in 1923, one of many laureates.

clue.text: Creepy-crawly let loose after return of stick insect

indicators.note: after means the loose letters come behind the insect
return of means the stick word is read backwards

parts.note: a rod is a stick
a bee is an insect

indicators.note: loose means the letters of let are set free into another order

explanation.surface: An insect lets a stick insect loose after it comes back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stick insect' reads as one creature, but splits: the stick turned round, then a separate insect.
explanation.definitionFit: A dung-eating black beetle of Europe, a bug of the kind loosely called a creepy-crawly.
